parts.label: Part 1
parts.article:
Part one. You will hear a woman phoning a holiday center to inquire about an activity holiday for her children.

First, you will have some time to look at questions one to six.

Now listen carefully and answer questions one to six.

Hello. Uh, could I speak to Mr. John Girdlestone, please?

Speaking.

Oh, hi. Uh, my name is Julie Bloom. I'm studying here in the UK for a year, and a friend told me you organize an international club where people of different nationalities can meet up.

That's right. The club was founded over fifty years ago, and at present, we've got members from approximately thirty countries. What's the name of your friend?

Louise. She's back in the States now.

Oh, Louise. I remember her. So, are you from the States too, Julie?

Yes, from California.

Great. Well, let's see what I can tell you about the club. It doesn't cost a lot to become a member. You can join for two months for two pounds fifty, or it's eight pounds fifty for twelve months.

And is it only for university students?

No, we're open to anyone. We have quite a few members from the language schools in town and also local people who are interested in meeting people from other countries.

Okay. So what sorts of things do you do?

Well, one thing we organize on a regular basis is dancing. That's a great way to get to know people.

Do you mean like disco?

[chuckles] No, we don't do disco. We do folk dances, some from Europe, but some from further afield. Everyone really enjoys them. We meet on Monday evenings at eight thirty. Do you know the University Center?

Yes, I think so.

We meet there in the main hall. Uh, don't get confused with the old hall where there's a ballroom dancing group. They're nothing to do with us.

And can I just show up?

Sure. Everyone's welcome.

And, uh, do I need to come along with a partner for the dancing?

You don't have to, though you can if you want to. I'm sure you'll have a good time. We have live music for some sessions. Um, I don't suppose you play a musical instrument, do you?

I play the violin, but I'm not very good.

Well, we're looking for some people to join the band. If you're interested, why don't you call Mike? His number's oh one three five six eight nine oh six seven four.

Okay. Thanks.

Uh, then we also have a meal together regularly. That's once a month, and it's always on a Sunday, the second one of the month.

Oh, so that'll be this coming Sunday. And where's that held?

In the University Center again, in the canteen. We used to have it in the restaurant on the ground floor, but that's closed at weekends now, unfortunately, so we're up on the top floor. They do very reasonably priced meals, things like baked potatoes and pizza.

And can I just show up there?

Absolutely.

Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions seven to ten.

Now listen and answer questions seven to ten.

Then we have some special summer events too. On July the second, we're going to a place called Great Hampton, about half an hour's drive away, to take part in the carnival they hold there every year. It's always a good day out, especially if it's a sunny day.

Oh, Louise said she went on that last year. She said it was really good, and it'd be nice to go somewhere out of town.

Well, in that case, you might be interested in our event on July the sixteenth. That's a walk in the Stanard Hills. We do about fifteen kilometers, so it's a decent walk, and it's for charity.

Uh, sounds a pretty long way.

Then on August the seventh, we're having a garden party at the home of one of our organizers. She has an outdoor pool. So if the weather's warm enough, you'll be able to go swimming.

Okay. Hard to imagine that today.

Well, the summer hasn't really started yet. Then our last summer event's on September the fourth. Last year, we went to a castle, but this year, we're going to the theater. We do ask members to let us know in advance for that so we can book.

Sure. Well, I'd definitely [phone dings] like to join.

That is the end of part one. You now have one minute to check your answers to part one.

analyses.content: 录音明确提到12个月（即一年）的费用是8.50英镑。
It doesn't cost a lot to become a member. You can join for two months for two pounds fifty, or it's eight pounds fifty for twelve months.
你可能会听到“两个月2.50英镑”而错填2.50，要注意题目问的是一年（a year / twelve months）的费用。
Do you know the University Center? Yes, I think so. We meet there in the main hall. Uh, don't get confused with the old hall, where there's a ballroom dancing group. They're nothing to do with us.
你可能会听到紧接着的“old hall”而填错，但录音特意强调了不要和那里搞混，因为那是另一个组织的活动场地。
录音中男生直接说明了碰面的地点是在大学中心的“主厅（main hall）”。
And, uh, do I need to come along with a partner for the dancing? You don't have to, though you can if you want to.
这道题的答案直接在女生的提问中给出了，你要注意听男生紧随其后的否定回答来确认。
女生提问跳舞是否需要带舞伴（partner），男生回答说不需要（don't have to）。
Well, we're looking for some people to join the band. If you're interested, why don't you call Mike? His number's oh one three five six eight nine oh six seven four.
前面虽然讨论了乐器（violin），但题目问的是需要人加入的具体组织，听到“join the”时直接抓取后面的名词即可。
录音明确说明他们正在找人加入乐队（band），并给出了联系人Mike的电话号码。
Uh, then we also have a meal together regularly. That's once a month, and it's always on a Sunday, the second one of the month.
你可能会听到“once a month”就想填once，但题目问的是具体哪一个“Sunday”。
录音说明聚餐是在每个月的第二个（second）星期天。
录音解释说现在食堂聚餐改到了顶层（top floor）。

In the University Center again, in the canteen. We used to have it in the restaurant on the ground floor, but that's closed at weekends now, unfortunately, so we're up on the top floor. They do very reasonably priced meals, things like baked potatoes and pizza.
你可能会听到“ground floor（一层）”就直接写上去，但录音紧接着用“but”转折，说明一层周末关门，现在改去了顶层。

Then we have some special summer events too. On July the second, we're going to a place called Great Hampton, about half an hour's drive away, to take part in the carnival they hold there every year. It's always a good day out, especially if it's a sunny day.
题目已经给出了时间和地点，你需要集中注意力听他们去那里参加的“活动名称”。
录音提到7月2日去Great Hampton是为了参加那里每年举办的嘉年华（carnival）。
Well, in that case, you might be interested in our event on July the sixteenth. That's a walk in the Stanard Hills. We do about fifteen kilometers, so it's a decent walk, and it's for charity.
听到15公里（fifteen kilometers）的定位词后，要注意听表示目的的介词“for”，直接抓取后面的名词。
录音明确指出这个15公里的步行活动是为了慈善（charity）。
Then on August the seventh, we're having a garden party at the home of one of our organizers. She has an outdoor pool, so if the weather's warm enough, you'll be able to go swimming.
你可能会听到前面的“outdoor pool”想填pool，但题目横线前是动词go，固定搭配只能是go swimming。
录音中提到如果天气够暖和，大家可以去游泳（swimming）。
Then our last summer event's on September the fourth. Last year, we went to a castle, but this year, we're going to the theater. We do ask members to let us know in advance for that so we can book.
你可能会听到“castle（城堡）”就填上去，但录音明确说了那是去年的活动（Last year），今年（this year）改去剧院了。
录音中对比了去年的活动，明确表示今年9月4日要去剧院（theater）。
